'''Sandra Cauffman''' (born May 10, 1962) is a Costa Rican-American (born in [[Costa Rica]]) specialist in electrical engineering and physics. She is known for her work at [[NASA]] in different projects. Her profile has been highlighted by [[UN Women]] for being a positive example for women, especially, youth and children.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url= http://beijing20.unwomen.org/en/news-and-events/stories/2014/5/woa-costa-rica-sandra-cauffman |title= Sandra Cauffman: From Costa Rica to Mars |date=20 May 2014 |website= Beijing+20 |publisher=UN Women |access-date= 21 July 2016}}</ref> Cauffman worked for 25 years at the NASA [[Goddard Space Flight Center]] in Greenbelt, MD in missions such as the mission to [[Mars]] [[MAVEN]], and [[Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite]] [[GOES-R]]. She is currently the Deputy Director of the Astrophysics Division within the [[Science Mission Directorate]] at NASA Headquarters in Washington, D.C. She served as the Deputy Director for the Earth Science Division from May 2016 - October 2021.  She served as Acting Director in the Earth Science Division from February 2019 to June 2020. Cauffman started as a contractor with NASA on February 1, 1988, and became a NASA employee February 11, 1991.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url =http://www.nacion.com/vivir/ciencia/Tica-Sandra-Cauffman-puesto-NASA_0_1562643763.html |title=Tica Sandra Cauffman asume alto cargo en NASA |date=23 May 2016 |website=La Nación |language=es |access-date=2016-05-30}}</ref> Cauffman is the first Costa Rican woman to lead a Mars-related mission.<ref>{{Cite news |url= http://www.revistaperfil.com/gente/Sandra-Cauffman-compartira-valentia-costarricenses_0_841715825.html |title=Sandra Cauffman compartirá su valentía con líderes costarricenses |last=González |first=Andrea |date=4 November 2015 |work=Revista Perfil |language=es |access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Cauffman, daughter of María Jerónima Rojas, was born in Costa Rica in a one-parent home of very scarce resources in [[Hatillo District|Hatillo]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nacion.com/ocio/revista-dominical/Sandra-Cauffman-Duena-destino_0_1383061709.html|title=Sandra Cauffman: Dueña de su destino|website=www.nacion.com|access-date=2016-05-30}}</ref> She grew up extremely poor, but refused to give up her love for [[Outline of space science|space science]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nacion.com/vivir/ciencia/ideas-compartidas-poderosas_0_1447055323.html|title=Sandra Cauffman: En la vida hay que soñar alto, pero también actuar|last=Vargas|first=Alejandra|date=24 October 2014|work=La Nacion|language=es|access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> Cauffman had been inspired by the [[Apollo 11|first Moon landing]] and recalled that she told her mother that she too, wanted to go to the Moon.<ref name=":2" /> Cauffman recalls that she had a difficult childhood, moving often and with her mother working two or three jobs at a time.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=http://www.ticotimes.net/2014/09/19/meet-sandra-cauffman-the-tica-co-directing-nasas-current-mission-to-mars|title=Meet Sandra Cauffman, the Tica co-directing NASA's current mission to Mars|last=Fendt|first=Lindsay|date=19 September 2014|work=The Tico Times|access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> Her mother, however, supported Cauffman's dreams and whenever Cauffman thought things were too hard, she looked to her mother for inspiration.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|url=http://elpais.com/elpais/2016/06/01/actualidad/1464766141_735211.html|title=Sandra soñó con ir a la luna y aterrizó en las estrellas|last=Manzano|first=Gador|date=2 June 2016|work=El Pais|language=es|access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref>

Mrs. Cauffman has been awarded the NASA the [[NASA Exceptional Achievement Medal|Exceptional Achievement Medal]]  and she is a three-time recipient of the [[NASA Outstanding Leadership Medal]]. She is also a four times recipient of the NASA Acquisition Improvement Award, and numerous GSFC and HQ awards.  She is a Senior Fellow on the [[Council for Excellence in Government]]. She is an Honorary Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], Costa Rica. She is also an Honorary Member of the Colegio Federado de Ingenieros y de Arquitectos in Costa Rica. Due to her extensive work in outreach and STEM in Costa Rica and Latin America the Government of Costa Rica issued a stamp in her honor in 2017. Cauffman attended the [[University of Costa Rica]] before transferring to [[George Mason University]].  She received a B.S. in physics, a B.S in electrical engineering and a M.S. in electrical engineering, all from George Mason University.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=21 September 2014 |title=Mars Wish: Mason Alumna Makes NASA Dream Come True |work=Mason Spirit |url=https://spirit.gmu.edu/2014/09/mars-wish-mason-alumna-makes-nasa-dream-come-true/ |access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> At George Mason, she learned English.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2 June 2016 |title=Diario 'El País' le dedica amplio reportaje a la tica Sandra Cauffman de la NASA |language=es |work=Teletica |url=http://www.teletica.com/Noticias/126790-Diario-El-Pais-le-dedica-amplio-reportaje-a-la-tica-Sandra-Cauffman-de-la-NASA.note.aspx |access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref>  GMU honored Ms. Cauffman achievements at their 50th Anniversary in 2018 as one of the 50 “exemplars”, alumni who exemplify the impact of a Mason degree around the world.

== Career ==
Sandra Cauffman has worked on many missions at NASA. Previously she was the Deputy Project Manager for the Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution mission (MAVEN),<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.revistaperfil.com/mujeres_que_inspiran/Sandra-Cauffman-Guia-espacial-esperanza_0_593940602.html|title=Sandra Cauffman. Guía espacial para creer en la esperanza|last=Fernanda Cruz|first=María|date=17 September 2014|work=Revista Perfil|language=es|access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> a mission to the red planet to its atmosphere. With this position, she became widely recognized in her native country, Costa Rica.<ref>{{cite web |author=NASA Goddard |date=2012-04-26 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JNEQUVPQUpA |title=MAVEN Profiles: Sandra Cauffman |website=[[YouTube]] |access-date=2016-05-26}}</ref>

Afterwards, she worked as Deputy Systems Program Director for the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites-R ([[GOES-R]]). Currently she is the Deputy Director of [[NASA]]'s Division of Earth Sciences.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Costa Rican Engineer Named New Assistant Director at NASA |url=http://www.costaricantimes.com/costa-rican-engineer-named-new-assistant-director-at-nasa/46544 |newspaper=Costa Rican Times |date=24 May 2016 |access-date=10 July 2016 }}</ref> From February 2019 until June 2020, she was Acting Director of the Earth Science Division.

As of 2014, she was only one of 4 Costa Ricans working directly for NASA.<ref name=":1" /> On many of the projects she worked on, including the [[Hubble Space Telescope|Hubble Space Telescope Servicing Mission 1]], she was often one of few female engineers on the team.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://spirit.gmu.edu/2015/04/mission-control/|title=Mission Control|last=Rich|first=Colleen Kearney|date=21 April 2015|work=Mason Spirit|access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> Cauffman gave a Young [[TED (conference)|TEDx]] talk in 2014 to inspire young people to dream.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.teletica.com/Noticias/69657-Sandra-Cauffman-nos-invita-a-sonar.note.aspx|title=Sandra Cauffman nos invita a soñar|date=22 October 2014|work=Teletica|language=es|access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> Cauffman wants all young people to believe that even if they have come from a poor family, that they can still reach their goals.<ref name=":4" /> After her retirement, she is planning to help support [[Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics|STEM]] for young people in Costa Rica.<ref name=":3" /> In 2016, Cauffman helped six high-school students from Costa Rica to visit [[Cape Canaveral]] as VIP guests for the launch of the GOES satellite.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.ticotimes.net/2016/03/08/costa-rican-students-get-the-surprise-of-a-lifetime-a-trip-to-nasa|title=Costa Rican students get the surprise of a lifetime: a trip to NASA|last=Stanley|first=Katherine|date=8 March 2016|work=The Tico Times|access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref>

In 2023, the University of Costa Rica conferred the title of Doctorate Honoris Causa for her contributions to [[research and development]] in science and technology, as well as the impulse she has given to young Costa Ricans, and especially women, to venture into these areas of knowledge.” The ceremony took place on March 8, 2023, celebrating [[International Women's Day|international women’s day]]. She is the fourth women distinguished with this title.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sandra Cauffman recibirá máxima distinción de la UCR |url=https://www.cu.ucr.ac.cr/inicio/noticias/noticia/Articulo/sandra-cauffam-recibira-maxima-distincion-de-la-ucr.html |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=www.cu.ucr.ac.cr |language=es-CR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Videos UCR |url=https://www.ucr.ac.cr/multimedios/videos/entrega-del-titulo-doctora-honoris-causa-sandra-cauffman.html |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=Universidad de Costa Rica |language=es}}</ref>
